31# Tile selection is done on the host so that the launch grid stays a *constant 

32# tuple* (never a ``lambda``): on the xpubin backend a callable grid object is 

33# baked into the compilation cache key, so a per-call lambda forces a full 

34# recompilation on every launch (KERNEL_OPT_EXPERIENCE #41). 

35# 

36# The kernel is compiled with a ``DIVISIBLE_*`` constexpr specialization: when 

37# every dimension is an exact multiple of the tile, the loads/stores are fully 

38# affine and mask-free, which is what lets ``tl.dot`` lower to the XDNN 

39# hardware matmul path. A masked 2D load inside a dot kernel -- even with an 

40# all-true mask and ``other=0.0`` -- silently miscompiles and/or blocks the 

41# block-DMA lowering (KERNEL_OPT_EXPERIENCE #17 / #36), so the masked path is 

42# reserved for the small, non-divisible shapes of the functional test matrix. 

43# 

44# fp32 GEMM forbids a large K-tile: BK=256 silently produces garbage 

45# (KERNEL_OPT_EXPERIENCE #19), so fp32 (and the bf16 path, which upcasts to 

46# fp32) is capped at BK=128 while fp16 may use BK=256. 

47_TILE_LARGE = 256 

48_TILE_MED = 128 

49_TILE_SMALL = 16 

50_NUM_WARPS = 4 

51 

52 

53@triton.jit 

54def _bmm_kernel( 

55 A, 

56 B, 

57 O, 

58 M, 

59 N, 

60 K, 

61 stride_ab, 

62 stride_am, 

63 stride_ak, 

64 stride_bb, 

65 stride_bk, 

66 stride_bn, 

67 stride_ob, 

68 stride_om, 

69 stride_on, 

70 TILE_M: tl.constexpr, 

71 TILE_N: tl.constexpr, 

72 TILE_K: tl.constexpr, 

73 DIVISIBLE_M: tl.constexpr, 

74 DIVISIBLE_N: tl.constexpr, 

75 DIVISIBLE_K: tl.constexpr, 

76): 

77 pid_b = ext.program_id(2) 

78 A += pid_b * stride_ab 

79 B += pid_b * stride_bb 

80 O += pid_b * stride_ob 

81 

82 pid_m = ext.program_id(0) 

83 pid_n = ext.program_id(1) 

84 

85 offs_m = pid_m * TILE_M + tl.arange(0, TILE_M) 

86 offs_n = pid_n * TILE_N + tl.arange(0, TILE_N) 

87 offs_k = tl.arange(0, TILE_K) 

88 

89 a_ptrs = A + offs_m[:, None] * stride_am + offs_k[None, :] * stride_ak 

90 b_ptrs = B + offs_k[:, None] * stride_bk + offs_n[None, :] * stride_bn 

91 o_ptrs = O + offs_m[:, None] * stride_om + offs_n[None, :] * stride_on 

92 

93 o = tl.zeros((TILE_M, TILE_N), dtype=tl.float32) 

94 

95 if DIVISIBLE_M and DIVISIBLE_N and DIVISIBLE_K: 

96 for _ in range(0, K // TILE_K): 

97 a = tl.load(a_ptrs) 

98 b = tl.load(b_ptrs) 

99 a_ptrs += TILE_K * stride_ak 

100 b_ptrs += TILE_K * stride_bk 

101 o += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False) 

102 tl.store(o_ptrs, o.to(O.dtype.element_ty)) 

103 else: 

104 mask_m = offs_m < M 

105 mask_n = offs_n < N 

106 for _ in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, TILE_K)): 

107 mask_k = offs_k < K 

108 mask_a = mask_m[:, None] & mask_k[None, :] 

109 mask_b = mask_k[:, None] & mask_n[None, :] 

110 a = tl.load(a_ptrs, mask_a, other=0.0) 

111 b = tl.load(b_ptrs, mask_b, other=0.0) 

112 offs_k += TILE_K 

113 a_ptrs += TILE_K * stride_ak 

114 b_ptrs += TILE_K * stride_bk 

115 o += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False) 

116 mask_c = mask_m[:, None] & mask_n[None, :] 

117 tl.store(o_ptrs, o.to(O.dtype.element_ty), mask_c)

120def _select_tile(M, K, dtype): 

121 """Pick a tile so the (square) benchmark shapes land on the mask-free path. 

122 

123 All benchmark shapes (256/384/512/1024/2048/4096) are multiples of 128, so 

124 they compile to the fast affine specialization; only the tiny functional 

125 shapes (M in {2, 8, 16, 32}) fall back to the masked small tile. 

126 

127 The XDNN block-DMA lowering is tuned for a ``load-tile-size=131072`` 

128 working set, so an asymmetric (TM, TN) = (512, 256) tile (131072 elements) 

129 is ~1.1-1.25x faster than the square 256x256 tile for M >= 1024. For 

130 M = 512 the asymmetric tile collapses the grid to (1, 2) programs and 

131 regresses, so keep the square 256x256 tile there. 

132 """ 

133 if M >= 1024 and M % 512 == 0: 

134 tm, tn = 512, 256 

135 elif M % _TILE_LARGE == 0: 

136 tm = tn = _TILE_LARGE 

137 elif M % _TILE_MED == 0: 

138 tm = tn = _TILE_MED 

139 else: 

140 tm = tn = _TILE_SMALL 

141 

142 if dtype == torch.float16: 

143 tk_opts = (_TILE_LARGE, _TILE_MED, _TILE_SMALL) 

144 else: 

145 # fp32 (and the bf16 path, which upcasts to fp32) must avoid BK=256. 

146 tk_opts = (_TILE_MED, _TILE_SMALL) 

147 

148 tk = _TILE_SMALL 

149 for cand in tk_opts: 

150 if K % cand == 0: 

151 tk = cand 

152 break 

153 return tm, tn, tk

156def _bmm(A, B, out=None): 

157 """Batched matmul for contiguous 3D (batch, M, K) x (batch, K, N). 

158 

159 When ``out`` is provided (a contiguous 3D tensor of the result shape and 

160 dtype) the product is written directly into it, avoiding an extra copy. 

161 """ 

162 batch, M, K = A.shape 

163 N = B.shape[2] 

164 if out is None: 

165 out = torch.empty((batch, M, N), dtype=A.dtype, device=A.device) 

166 

167 tm, tn, tk = _select_tile(M, K, A.dtype) 

168 grid = (triton.cdiv(M, tm), triton.cdiv(N, tn), batch) 

169 if A.device.index == torch_device_fn.current_device(): 

170 _bmm_kernel[grid]( 

171 A, 

172 B, 

173 out, 

174 M, 

175 N, 

176 K, 

177 A.stride(0), 

178 A.stride(1), 

179 A.stride(2), 

180 B.stride(0), 

181 B.stride(1), 

182 B.stride(2), 

183 out.stride(0), 

184 out.stride(1), 

185 out.stride(2), 

186 TILE_M=tm, 

187 TILE_N=tn, 

188 TILE_K=tk, 

189 DIVISIBLE_M=(M % tm == 0), 

190 DIVISIBLE_N=(N % tn == 0), 

191 DIVISIBLE_K=(K % tk == 0), 

192 num_warps=_NUM_WARPS, 

193 ) 

194 else: 

195 with torch_device_fn.device(A.device): 

196 _bmm_kernel[grid]( 

197 A, 

198 B, 

199 out, 

200 M, 

201 N, 

202 K, 

203 A.stride(0), 

204 A.stride(1), 

205 A.stride(2), 

206 B.stride(0), 

207 B.stride(1), 

208 B.stride(2), 

209 out.stride(0), 

210 out.stride(1), 

211 out.stride(2), 

212 TILE_M=tm, 

213 TILE_N=tn, 

214 TILE_K=tk, 

215 DIVISIBLE_M=(M % tm == 0), 

216 DIVISIBLE_N=(N % tn == 0), 

217 DIVISIBLE_K=(K % tk == 0), 

218 num_warps=_NUM_WARPS, 

219 ) 

220 return out

223def _cast_dtype(x, dtype, out=None): 

224 """Dtype-converting copy via the backend's tuned contiguous-cast kernel. 

225 

226 The cast must round fp32->bf16 with round-to-nearest-even, exactly as 

227 ``torch.matrix_power``'s bf16 chain does, otherwise the per-step rounding 

228 of ``_matrix_power_bf16`` drifts from the reference. ``_to_copy_contiguous`` 

229 (``_kunlunxin/ops/to.py``) is the backend's own Triton cast path: its 

230 fp32->bf16 kernel implements RNE with the ``0x7FFF + lsb`` bit bias, which 

231 is bit-identical to ``Tensor.to``, and its bf16->fp32 path is an exact 

232 upcast. It is a real gems kernel (no ATen/native copy fallback), unlike the 

233 previously used ATen ``_copy_from`` strided-copy primitive, which the 

234 fallback rule now forbids. 

235 

236 When ``out`` is provided the result is written directly into it. 

237 """ 

238 if out is None: 

239 out = torch.empty(x.shape, dtype=dtype, device=x.device) 

240 if dtype == torch.bfloat16 and x.is_floating_point() and x.dtype != torch.bfloat16: 

241 # fp32 -> bf16 (and fp16 -> bf16): `_to_copy_contiguous` routes every 

242 # ->bf16 cast through a 256-element tile (its conservative safe path), 

243 # which serializes a 16.7M-element cast into ~65k tiny launches and is 

244 # ~16x slower than necessary. The RNE bit-manipulation kernel is 

245 # verified bit-identical to ``Tensor.to(bf16)`` at large tiles 

246 # (probe_cast_tile), so launch it directly with the same power-of-two 

247 # tile the bf16->fp32 upcast already enjoys. 

248 _cast_to_bf16(x, out) 

249 else: 

250 _to_copy_contiguous(x, out, dtype) 

251 return out 

252 

253 

254def _cast_to_bf16(x, out): 

255 """fp32 -> bf16 round-to-nearest-even cast via a large-tile direct launch.""" 

256 n = x.numel() 

257 if n == 0: 

258 return out 

259 block = 1 << (n - 1).bit_length() if n > 1 else 1 

260 if block > 16384: 

261 block = 16384 

262 grid = ((n + block - 1) // block,) 

263 if x.device.index == torch_device_fn.current_device(): 

264 _to_copy_contiguous_to_bf16_kernel[grid](x, out, n, block) 

265 else: 

266 with torch_device_fn.device(x.device): 

267 _to_copy_contiguous_to_bf16_kernel[grid](x, out, n, block) 

268 return out 

269

271@triton.jit 

272def _round_to_bf16_kernel(inp, out, n_elements, BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr): 

273 """Round fp32 to bf16 precision (RNE) and return as fp32, in one 1D pass. 

274 

275 The bf16 power chain needs a ``fp32 -> bf16 -> fp32`` roundtrip after every 

276 squaring product. Doing it as a single elementwise kernel (read fp32, 

277 write fp32) halves the memory traffic of the two-kernel roundtrip and keeps 

278 the bit manipulation out of the dot kernel (where it miscompiles / is ~10x 

279 slow -- the ``_round_fp32_to_bf16`` epilogue experiment). 

280 """ 

281 offsets = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

282 mask = offsets < n_elements 

283 values = tl.load(inp + offsets, mask=mask).to(tl.float32) 

284 fp32_bits = values.to(tl.uint32, bitcast=True) 

285 rounding_bias = 0x7FFF + ((fp32_bits >> 16) & 1) 

286 out_bits = ((fp32_bits + rounding_bias) >> 16) << 16 

287 tl.store(out + offsets, out_bits.to(tl.float32, bitcast=True), mask=mask) 

288 

289 

290# The RNE round is compute-bound (bit manipulation), but routing it through the 

291# tuned pointwise_dynamic codegen with the async-DMA config (the same recipe as 

292# ``_to_copy_func_async`` in ``to.py``) still yields a ~1.25x win on the large 

293# benchmark shapes by overlapping the load/store stream (verified bit-identical 

294# to the plain kernel above for M in {384..4096}). Small shapes keep the plain 

295# big-tile kernel: pointwise_dynamic's host-side prep dominates the ~5us of 

296# device work on the tiny functional-test shapes. 

297_async_round_config = CodeGenConfig( 

298 512, 

299 (65536, 65536, 65536), 

300 32, 

301 True, 

302 prefer_1d_tile=True, 

303 isCloseMemoryAsync=False, 

304 kunlunAutoGrid=True, 

305) 

306 

307 

308@pointwise_dynamic( 

309 is_tensor=[ 

310 True, 

311 ], 

312 promotion_methods=[(0, "DEFAULT")], 

313 config=_async_round_config, 

314) 

315@triton.jit 

316def _round_to_bf16_async(x): 

317 fp32_bits = x.to(tl.uint32, bitcast=True) 

318 rounding_bias = 0x7FFF + ((fp32_bits >> 16) & 1) 

319 out_bits = ((fp32_bits + rounding_bias) >> 16) << 16 

320 return out_bits.to(tl.float32, bitcast=True) 

321 

322 

323def _round_bf16(x): 

324 """Round a fp32 tensor to bf16 precision, returned as fp32 again.""" 

325 out = torch.empty(x.shape, dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device) 

326 n = x.numel() 

327 if n == 0: 

328 return out 

329 # The async pointwise_dynamic path wins on device time (~1.25x) but its 

330 # host-side prep (~13us/call of Python) makes the whole bf16 chain 

331 # host-bound on the small shapes (M <= 1024). Route only the >= 2M-element 

332 # shapes (2048x2048 and up) through it, where the device-work saving 

333 # exceeds the host overhead; small shapes keep the plain big-tile kernel. 

334 if n >= 2 * 1024 * 1024: 

335 _round_to_bf16_async(x, out0=out) 

336 return out 

337 block = 1 << (n - 1).bit_length() if n > 1 else 1 

338 if block > 16384: 

339 block = 16384 

340 grid = ((n + block - 1) // block,) 

341 if x.device.index == torch_device_fn.current_device(): 

342 _round_to_bf16_kernel[grid](x, out, n, block) 

343 else: 

344 with torch_device_fn.device(x.device): 

345 _round_to_bf16_kernel[grid](x, out, n, block) 

346 return out

349def _matrix_power_bf16(A, n, out=None): 

350 """Repeated-squaring for bf16 via fp32 gemm kernels. 

351 

352 ``tl.dot`` on this backend does not round a bf16 matmul the same way 

353 ``torch.matrix_power``'s bf16 chain does: loading bf16 inside a dot kernel 

354 is mis-compiled (KERNEL_OPT_EXPERIENCE #11), and the residual per-product 

355 error is amplified 2x per squaring step, blowing the bf16 tolerance. 

356 Matching torch's semantics (each repeated-squaring product is rounded back 

357 to bf16) is done by upcasting the bf16 matrix to fp32 *once*, running the 

358 fp32 gemm, and rounding every intermediate product back to bf16 on the host 

359 via a single fused ``fp32->bf16->fp32`` elementwise kernel 

360 (``_round_to_bf16_kernel``). This keeps the kernel fp32-only (no bf16 load) 

361 while reproducing torch's per-step bf16 rounding. 

362 

363 When ``out`` is provided the final result is downcast directly into it. 

364 """ 

365 batch, M, _ = A.shape 

366 

367 if n == 0: 

368 eye = torch.eye(M, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=A.device) 

369 res = eye.unsqueeze(0).expand(batch, M, M).contiguous() 

370 if out is not None: 

371 out.copy_(res) 

372 res = out 

373 return res 

374 

375 if n == 1: 

376 res = A.clone() 

377 if out is not None: 

378 out.copy_(res) 

379 res = out 

380 return res 

381 

382 # Upcast once: bf16 -> fp32 is exact, and the kernel never loads bf16. 

383 base = _cast_dtype(A, torch.float32) 

384 result = None 

385 while n > 0: 

386 if n & 1: 

387 # ``base`` is always bf16-representable (exact upcast of a bf16 

388 # value, or the rounded output of a previous squaring step), so the 

389 # first accumulation needs no extra rounding step. 

390 if result is None: 

391 result = base 

392 else: 

393 prod = _bmm(result, base) 

394 if (n >> 1) == 0: 

395 # Final accumulation: the fp32->bf16 RNE downcast composes 

396 # the ``_round_bf16`` roundtrip with the final downcast (the 

397 # round already leaves the value bf16-representable), so fuse 

398 # both into a single launch and skip the extra round kernel. 

399 return _cast_dtype(prod, torch.bfloat16, out=out) 

400 result = _round_bf16(prod) 

401 n >>= 1 

402 if n > 0: 

403 base = _round_bf16(_bmm(base, base)) 

404 return _cast_dtype(result, torch.bfloat16, out=out) 

405 

406 

407def _matrix_power(A, n, out=None): 

408 """Compute A ** n for a contiguous 3D stack of square matrices (batch, M, M). 

409 

410 When ``out`` is provided (a contiguous 3D tensor of the same shape/dtype) 

411 the result is written directly into it, avoiding a final copy. 

412 """ 

413 if n < 0: 

414 # Negative powers need an LU inverse, which torch only supports for 

415 # fp32/fp64. Delegate to the generic implementation (fp32 path). 

416 res = _generic_matrix_power(A, n) 

417 if out is not None: 

418 out.copy_(res) 

419 res = out 

420 return res 

421 

422 if A.dtype == torch.bfloat16: 

423 return _matrix_power_bf16(A, n, out=out) 

424 

425 if A.dtype == torch.float64: 

426 # Not exercised by tests/benchmark (fp16/fp32/bf16 only); keep the 

427 # generic gems path for completeness. 

428 res = _generic_matrix_power(A, n) 

429 if out is not None: 

430 out.copy_(res) 

431 res = out 

432 return res 

433 

434 batch, M, _ = A.shape 

435 

436 if n == 0: 

437 eye = torch.eye(M, dtype=A.dtype, device=A.device) 

438 res = eye.unsqueeze(0).expand(batch, M, M).contiguous() 

439 if out is not None: 

440 out.copy_(res) 

441 res = out 

442 return res 

443 

444 if n == 1: 

445 res = A.clone() 

446 if out is not None: 

447 out.copy_(res) 

448 res = out 

449 return res 

450 

451 result = None 

452 base = A 

453 while n > 0: 

454 if n & 1: 

455 if result is None: 

456 result = base 

457 else: 

458 # On the final accumulation write directly into ``out``. 

459 result = _bmm(result, base, out=(out if (n >> 1) == 0 else None)) 

460 n >>= 1 

461 if n > 0: 

462 base = _bmm(base, base) 

463 if out is not None and result is not out: 

464 out.copy_(result) 

465 result = out 

466 return result 

467

469def matrix_power(A, n): 

470 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN MATRIX_POWER") 

471 assert A.ndim >= 2, "matrix_power expects a tensor of at least 2 dimensions" 

472 assert A.shape[-1] == A.shape[-2], "matrix_power expects square matrices" 

473 assert A.dtype in [ 

474 torch.float16, 

475 torch.bfloat16, 

476 torch.float32, 

477 torch.float64, 

478 ], f"matrix_power only supports float16, bfloat16, float32, float64, got {A.dtype}" 

479 

480 M = A.shape[-1] 

481 batch_shape = A.shape[:-2] 

482 A3 = A.reshape(-1, M, M).contiguous() 

483 

484 out = _matrix_power(A3, n) 

485 return out.reshape(*batch_shape, M, M) 

486 

487 

488def matrix_power_out(A, n, *, out): 

489 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN MATRIX_POWER_OUT") 

490 assert A.ndim >= 2, "matrix_power expects a tensor of at least 2 dimensions" 

491 assert A.shape[-1] == A.shape[-2], "matrix_power expects square matrices" 

492 assert A.dtype in [ 

493 torch.float16, 

494 torch.bfloat16, 

495 torch.float32, 

496 torch.float64, 

497 ], f"matrix_power only supports float16, bfloat16, float32, float64, got {A.dtype}" 

498 

499 M = A.shape[-1] 

500 batch_shape = A.shape[:-2] 

501 A3 = A.reshape(-1, M, M).contiguous() 

502 

503 # Write the final product directly into ``out`` when it is a contiguous 

504 # buffer that does not alias the input; otherwise fall back to a copy so 

505 # aliasing/stride semantics stay identical to ``torch.matrix_power``. 

506 if out.is_contiguous() and out.dtype == A.dtype and out.data_ptr() != A.data_ptr(): 

507 out3 = out.reshape(-1, M, M) 

508 _matrix_power(A3, n, out=out3) 

509 return out 

510 

511 result = _matrix_power(A3, n) 

512 out.copy_(result.reshape(*batch_shape, M, M)) 

513 return out
